Approach: iterate over Unicode code points, extend the current run when the character matches, and otherwise append the completed run and start a new one. Append the final run after iteration. This takes O(n) time and O(r) output space for n code points and r runs.

Invariant: after each processed code point, the output contains all completed runs in order, and the current character and count describe exactly the unfinished trailing run.

Boundary cases: an empty string returns []; one character produces one run; all identical characters produce one run; alternating characters produce count-one runs. Nonadjacent repetitions stay separate, supplementary Unicode characters count as single code points, and combining marks remain separate code points rather than being grouped into grapheme clusters.
